verdict.rationale: Kick provides the building blocks — MCP/CLI access to query transactions and generate reports (kick-docs-15, kick-docs-24, kick-docs-29), a documented 'automate month-end checks' workflow, reconciliation logic that explicitly checks for 'no duplicates' (kick-supp-reconciliation), confidence-gated categorization that flags uncertain transactions for review (kick-supp-categorization), and an AI-inclusive audit trail (kick-supp-audit-trail). But there is no turnkey 'anomaly detection' or spend-flagging feature — an ai-native user would need to build this monitoring logic themselves via MCP queries rather than use a native pre-close anomaly report. Missing for 10: a documented anomaly-detection/alerting feature, evidence of proactive flagging before close (vs. manual reconciliation), and independent confirmation the MCP tools can reliably surface duplicates/spend outliers.
